title: Rumi on the Journey Home
subtitle: Eight Persian Sufi poems with English translation
yt_title: Rumi on the Journey Home | 8 Persian Sufi Poems with English Translation
intro: Rumi believed that every soul is a traveller, far from where it began.
The longing we feel is the pull of home.
Here are eight passages about the road back.

poems.name: What Place Is This?

lines.fa: گوهر پاک از کجا عالم خاک از کجا
lines.en: Where is the pure pearl from, and where the world of dust?

lines.fa: بر چه فرود آمدیت بار کنید این چه جاست
lines.en: Why did you come down here? Pack your loads: what place is this?

tafsir: Rumi speaks to souls as if they were travellers at an inn.
You are a pearl, he says. What are you doing in the dust?
Do not unpack here as if you were staying forever.
This world is a stop on the way, not the destination.

poems.name: Back Into the Sea

lines.fa: هر پاره کف جسم کز آن بحر نشان یافت
lines.en: Every fleck of the body's foam that caught a sign of that sea

lines.fa: در حال گدازید و در آن بحر روان شد
lines.en: melted at once and flowed back into that sea.

tafsir: Our bodies, Rumi says, are like foam on the surface of an ocean.
When the foam remembers the sea, it does not resist.
It melts and flows home.
The journey back is not a struggle. It is a remembering.

poems.name: Too Large for the Sky

lines.fa: تو آن ماهی که در گردون نگنجی
lines.en: You are the moon that does not fit inside the sky,

lines.fa: تو آن آبی که در جیحون نگنجی
lines.en: the water that does not fit inside the Oxus.

tafsir: The Oxus, the Jeyhun, was the great river of Rumi's homeland, near Balkh.
He says the Beloved is too large for any sky or river.
That is why no single place in this world feels completely like home.
We are travelling toward something bigger than every place.

poems.name: Saddle the Horse

lines.en: Without you, the whole wide sky has grown narrow;

lines.fa: هین براق وصال را زین کن
lines.en: come, saddle the steed of union.

tafsir: Buraq is the heavenly steed that carried the Prophet on his night journey.
Without the Beloved, even the sky feels cramped.
So Rumi asks for the swiftest horse in heaven.
Longing is impatient to be on the road.

poems.name: Beyond Both Worlds

lines.fa: چون نگه کردم سر من بود پر از عشق او
lines.en: When I looked, my head was full of his love;

lines.fa: من برون از هر دو عالم منظری را یافتم
lines.en: and beyond both worlds I found a place to look out from.

tafsir: Rumi looks inside himself and finds only love.
And from there, a window opens.
Not in this world, and not in the next, but beyond both.
Sometimes the journey home is simply looking inward.

poems.name: A Thirsty Man's Dream

lines.fa: تشنه چه بیند به خواب چشمه و حوض و سبو
lines.en: What does a thirsty man see in his dreams? A spring, a pool, a jug.

lines.fa: تشنه وصل توام کی بگذارم طواف
lines.en: I am thirsty for union with you: how could I stop circling?

tafsir: The thirsty dream of water, every night.
Rumi is thirsty for the Beloved, so he circles, like pilgrims around the Kaaba.
The circling is not wasted. It is how thirst prays.
Our longing keeps us turning toward home.

poems.name: My Soul Cries in Secret

lines.fa: آن دم که نهان شوی ز چشمم
lines.en: The moment you hide from my eyes,

tafsir: Some of Rumi's lines are very small, and very true.
When the Beloved is hidden, the soul weeps quietly.
Not loudly, not for others to see.
That secret crying is the compass that always points home.

poems.name: Watchman, Wake Up

lines.fa: ای دل سوی دلدار شو ای یار سوی یار شو
lines.en: O heart, go to the one who holds your heart; O friend, go to the Friend.

lines.fa: ای پاسبان بیدار شو خفته نشاید پاسبان
lines.en: O watchman, wake up: a watchman must not sleep.

tafsir: This is from Rumi's great caravan poem.
Everything is told to go where it belongs: the heart to its beloved, the friend to the Friend.
And the watchman inside us is told to stay awake.
The road home begins the moment we wake up to it. Thank you for travelling with us.

outro: Thank you for travelling with these verses.
